questions.question: The BHARAT study, launched by the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Bengaluru, in 2023, focuses on:

options.text: Studying biomarkers of healthy aging, resilience, adversity, and transitions
Promoting traditional wellness practices among senior citizens
Surveying rural health infrastructure for elderly care
Identifying economic patterns of India's aging population

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Studying biomarkers of healthy aging, resilience, adversity, and transitions**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **BHARAT study** (Biomarkers of Healthy Aging, Resilience, Adversity, and Transitions) was launched by the **Centre for Brain Research (CBR)**, an autonomous center of the **Indian Institute of Science (IISc)**, **Bengaluru**, in **2023**.
 
• The primary focus of this study is to identify **biological markers (biomarkers)** that correlate with **healthy brain aging** and to understand how certain individuals remain resilient against cognitive decline despite various adversities.
 
• It is a **longitudinal study**, meaning it tracks the same group of individuals over an extended period to observe changes in **cognitive health**, **brain structure**, and **lifestyle factors**.
 
• The initiative aims to address the growing challenge of **neurodegenerative disorders** such as **Alzheimer’s disease** and **dementia** within the specific context of the **Indian population**. ***Hence, the correct answer is option 1.***
 
• By studying the **resilience** and **transitions** of the aging brain, the researchers hope to develop better **diagnostic tools** and **preventative strategies** tailored to Indian genetics and lifestyle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Centre for Brain Research (CBR):** 
 
 
• The **CBR** was established at **IISc Bengaluru** through a generous philanthropic contribution from **Mr. Kris Gopalakrishnan**, the co-founder of **Infosys**.
 
• The center focuses on finding solutions for **brain-related disorders** that affect the elderly, particularly those leading to **cognitive impairment**.
 
 
 
• **Target Demographic:** 
 
 
• The **BHARAT study** typically recruits participants aged **45 years and above** to capture the early transitions into the aging phase.
 
• This demographic is critical because **pathological changes** in the brain often begin decades before **clinical symptoms** of dementia appear.
 
 
 
• **Methodology and Technology:** 
 
 
• The study employs state-of-the-art technologies, including **3-Tesla MRI scanners** for neuroimaging, **genomic sequencing**, and **proteomic analysis** from blood samples.
 
• Participants undergo rigorous **neuropsychological assessments** to evaluate memory, attention, and executive functions.
 
 
 
• **Significance for India:** 
 
 
• With India’s aging population expected to reach nearly **20%** of the total population by **2050**, research into **healthy aging** is a national priority.
 
• The study accounts for unique **Indian socio-economic factors**, **dietary habits**, and **environmental exposures** that differ significantly from the Western cohorts usually studied in global health research.
 
 
 
• **Longitudinal Cohort Studies:** 
 
 
• Similar to the **Srinivaspura Aging, Neuro Epidemiology and Genetics (SAGE)** study, BHARAT creates a massive **database** of clinical and biological data to serve as a resource for future **drug development** and **public health policy**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **IISc** was founded in **1909** and is consistently ranked as one of India's premier institutes for **scientific research**.
 
• According to the **Dementia in India 2020 report**, an estimated **5.3 million** people above age **60** had dementia in India, a number expected to double by **2050**.
 
• The **BHARAT study** contributes to the **Global Brain Health** initiative by providing data from the **Global South**, which is currently underrepresented in genomic and aging research.
 
• The term **"Biomarkers"** in this context refers to measurable indicators such as **blood proteins** or **brain volume** changes that can predict **disease risk**.
</ul

questions.question: Which four entertainment icons were honored with Oscars at the 2025 Governors Awards?

options.text: Tom Cruise, Dolly Parton, Debbie Allen, Wynn Thomas
George Lucas, Viola Davis, Michael Mann, Sofia Coppola
Meryl Streep, Judi Dench, Clint Eastwood, Martin Scorsese
Steven Spielberg, Angela Bassett, Benicio del Toro, Julie Taymor

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tom Cruise, Dolly Parton, Debbie Allen, and Wynn Thomas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences (AMPAS)** announced the recipients for the **15th Annual Governors Awards**, which are honorary Oscars recognizing extraordinary lifetime achievement in the film industry.
 
• **Tom Cruise** was selected to receive the **Jean Hersholt Humanitarian Award** for his extensive philanthropic efforts and his significant contributions to the global film industry, particularly his role in revitalizing theatrical exhibition in the **post-pandemic era**.
 
• **Dolly Parton**, a legendary **country music** singer, songwriter, and actress, was honored with an **Honorary Award** for her seven-decade-long career and her massive influence on film through music and screen presence, including her **Oscar-nominated** work in films like **9 to 5**.
 
• **Debbie Allen** was recognized with an **Honorary Award** for her multi-faceted career as a **director**, **choreographer**, and **actress**, acknowledging her legacy in dance-heavy productions and her mentorship through the **Debbie Allen Dance Academy**.
 
• **Wynn Thomas**, a trailblazing **production designer**, received an **Honorary Award** for his groundbreaking work in cinema, notably being the first **African American** production designer to achieve major acclaim through collaborations on films like **Do the Right Thing** and **A Beautiful Mind**.
 
• These icons were selected by the **Academy's Board of Governors** for their profound impact on the arts and sciences of motion pictures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Governors Awards:**
 
 
• The **Governors Awards** is an annual event held by **AMPAS** where three specific awards are presented: the **Honorary Award**, the **Jean Hersholt Humanitarian Award**, and the **Irving G. Thalberg Memorial Award**.
 
• Unlike the competitive Oscars, these are **non-competitive** awards decided by a vote of the **Board of Governors** to honor individuals who have made indelible marks on the industry over their entire careers.
 
 
 
• **The Jean Hersholt Humanitarian Award:**
 
 
• This award is given to an individual in the **motion picture industry** whose humanitarian efforts have brought credit to the industry.
 
• Notable past recipients include **Angelina Jolie**, **Oprah Winfrey**, and **Elizabeth Taylor**.
 
 
 
• **The Honorary Award:**
 
 
• The **Honorary Oscar** is given for "extraordinary distinction in lifetime achievement, exceptional contributions to the state of motion picture arts and sciences, or for outstanding service to the Academy."
 
• This award bypasses the traditional nomination process and is represented by the iconic **statuette**.
 
 
 
• **Timing and Significance:**
 
 
• The **Governors Awards** ceremony is typically held in **November** or **January**, separate from the main **Academy Awards** telecast, to allow for longer tributes to the legends of cinema.
 
• The **2025 cycle** of awards (presented in late **2024**) serves as a precursor to the **97th Academy Awards**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Tom Cruise**: Known for the **Mission: Impossible** franchise and **Top Gun: Maverick**, his award highlights his **stewardship** of the cinematic experience during the **COVID-19** crisis.
 
• **Dolly Parton**: Her **Imagination Library** and her **Grammy**-winning musical legacy have made her a global cultural ambassador.
 
• **Debbie Allen**: A former **Kennedy Center Honoree**, she has directed numerous episodes of **Grey's Anatomy** and starred in the iconic series **Fame**.
 
• **Wynn Thomas**: His work on **Hidden Figures** (2016) and **Malcolm X** (1992) showcases his ability to define the visual language of historical and contemporary stories.
</ul

questions.question: Who won the prestigious Women Player of the Year Female award for FIH 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Yibbi Jansen**__.

__
 
• The **International Hockey Federation (FIH)** officially announced the winners of the **FIH Hockey Stars Awards 2024** on **November 8, 2024**, naming **Yibbi Jansen** of the **Netherlands** as the **FIH Women Player of the Year**.
 
• **Yibbi Jansen** played an instrumental role in the **Netherlands** women's team securing the **gold medal** at the **Paris 2024 Olympics**.
 
• During the **Paris 2024 Olympic Games**, **Jansen** showcased her dominance by finishing as the tournament's **top scorer** with **9 goals**, primarily through her world-class **drag-flicking** expertise.
 
• She has been a consistent performer in the **FIH Pro League** and was a key factor in the Dutch team’s continued dominance in international hockey over the past year.
 
• The award is a testament to her technical skills and scoring ability, making her one of the most feared penalty corner specialists in the world.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Other Major FIH 2024 Award Winners:**
 
 
• **FIH Men's Player of the Year**: **Harmanpreet Singh**, the captain of the **Indian Men's Hockey Team**, won this award for the third time after leading **India** to a **bronze medal** at the **Paris 2024 Olympics** and finishing as the tournament's leading scorer with **10 goals**.
 
• **FIH Goalkeeper of the Year**: In the men's category, **PR Sreejesh** (India) was honored for his stellar performance in his final international season. In the women's category, **Ye Jiao** (China) won the award for her incredible saves that propelled **China** to an Olympic **silver medal**.
 
• **FIH Rising Star of the Year**: The women’s award went to **Zoe Diaz** of **Argentina**, while the men’s award was secured by **Sufyan Khan** of **Pakistan**.
 
• **FIH Coach of the Year**: **Alyson Annan** (China) was named the best women’s coach, and **Jeroen Delmee** (Netherlands) was named the best men’s coach.

• It was founded on **7 January 1924** in **Paris** to ensure hockey was included in the **Olympic Games**.
 
• The federation currently oversees major tournaments including the **Hockey World Cup**, the **FIH Pro League**, and the **Olympic hockey** competitions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Selection Process:** The **FIH Hockey Stars Awards** winners are determined by a comprehensive voting system that includes **National Associations** (represented by team captains and coaches), **fans**, **players**, and **media members**.
 
• **Dutch Dominance:** With **Yibbi Jansen** winning the **Player of the Year**, the **Netherlands** continues its streak of having at least one female player on the podium for over a decade, reflecting the country's status as a powerhouse in women's field hockey.
 
• **Sarah Wilson:** It is important to note that **Sarah Wilson** (Option 3) is a highly respected international **umpire** from **Scotland** and was not a candidate for the Player of the Year award.

• The election was conducted under the supervision of the **Election Commission of India**, which ensured that the **Model Code of Conduct** was followed throughout the campaigning and polling period.
 
• The **Trinamool Congress** candidate defeated the nearest rival from the **Bharatiya Janata Party** (**BJP**), marking a significant trend in the local political landscape of **West Bengal** during the **2025** mid-term assessments.

• Founded on **January 1, 1998**, by **Mamata Banerjee** after splitting from the Indian National Congress.
 
• The party has been in power in **West Bengal** since **2011**, ending the **34-year** rule of the Left Front.
 
• Its official election symbol is the **"Jora Ghas Phul"** (Twin Flowers in Grass), and it currently holds the status of a prominent state party with significant influence in national politics.

• These elections are essential for maintaining the full democratic representation of a constituency within the **legislature**.

This geographical location often makes issues like **border security**, **migration**, and **rural development** central to the election manifestos of parties like the **Trinamool Congress** and **BJP**.

questions.question: In which competition did Parul Chaudhary break her national record in 2025?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Parul Chaudhary**, the prominent Indian distance runner, showcased an exceptional performance at the **Asian Athletics Championship** in **2025**, where she successfully broke her previous **National Record**.
 
• She competes primarily in the **3000m steeplechase** and the **5000m** events, and her record-breaking feat in **2025** further solidified her position as one of **India**'s elite track athletes.
 
• The **Asian Athletics Championship** is a biennial event organized by the **Asian Athletics Association**, and the **2025** edition served as a crucial platform for athletes to qualify for the **World Athletics Championships**.
 
• During the competition, **Parul Chaudhary** demonstrated superior stamina and tactical awareness, surpassing the timing she had previously set at international meets like the **World Championships** and **Asian Games**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

questions.question: Which of the following neighboring countries of India had a ranking worse than India in the Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) Index in the 2025 edition of the Sustainable Development Report (SDR) released in June 2025?
questions.solution:
p>The correct answer is __**Pakistan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Sustainable Development Report (SDR) 2025**, released in **June 2025**, provides a comprehensive assessment of the progress made by **193 UN Member States** towards achieving the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**.
 
• In the **2025 edition** of the index, **India** secured a rank of **109th** globally. While India has shown progress in certain areas like climate action and basic infrastructure, it continues to face challenges in goals related to hunger, gender equality, and quality education.
 
• Among India's neighbors, **Pakistan** had a ranking significantly worse than India, placed at the **137th** position. This indicates that **Pakistan** is lagging behind in the majority of the **17 Sustainable Development Goals** compared to other South Asian nations.
 
• In contrast, other neighboring countries such as **Bhutan**, **Sri Lanka**, and **Nepal** performed better than India in the **2025 SDR**. **Bhutan** usually maintains a high rank due to its focus on environmental conservation and social well-being, while **Nepal** and **Sri Lanka** have shown resilience in social indicators despite economic fluctuations.
 
• The **Sustainable Development Index** score for **India** was approximately **64.0**, whereas **Pakistan** scored lower, reflecting a wider gap in achieving the **2030 Agenda** targets.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN):**
 
 
• The **SDR** is published annually by the **UN Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN)**, which has been operating under the auspices of the **UN Secretary-General** since **2012**.
 
• The report is led by **Professor Jeffrey Sachs** and provides a data-driven ranking to help countries identify gaps in their **sustainable development** strategies.
 
 
 
• **The 17 SDGs:**
 
 
• The **Sustainable Development Goals** were adopted by all **United Nations Member States** in **2015** as a universal call to action to end poverty, protect the planet, and ensure peace and prosperity by **2030**.
 
• Key goals include **Goal 1: No Poverty**, **Goal 5: Gender Equality**, **Goal 13: Climate Action**, and **Goal 16: Peace, Justice, and Strong Institutions**.
 
 
 
• **Regional Performance in South Asia:**
 
 
• South Asia remains a region with diverse performance levels. While **Bhutan** and **Maldives** often lead the regional charts, **Pakistan** and **Afghanistan** consistently rank at the bottom due to political instability and economic crises.
 
• **India's** performance is critical to the global success of the **SDGs** because of its massive population and **economic footprint**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **SDG Index** score can be interpreted as the percentage of **SDG achievement**. A score of **100** indicates that all goals have been fully met.
 
• For the **2025 report**, the global average progress has been noted as stagnant or slow since **2020**, primarily due to the long-term impacts of global health crises and geopolitical conflicts.
 
• **Finland**, **Sweden**, and **Denmark** continue to occupy the **top three positions** in the global rankings for **2025**, having achieved or being on track to achieve most of the targets.
 
• The **June 2025** report emphasizes the need for increased **financial architecture reform** to help developing nations like **India** and **Pakistan** bridge the funding gap required for **green transitions** and **social safety nets**.
</ul

• **BluSmart:** Recognized as a pioneer in **all-electric ride-sharing** in **India**, it operated a large fleet and massive **charging hubs**. Its closure in the **2025** timeline created a ripple effect in the **green mobility** market, leading to concerns over **unrecovered user funds**.
 
• **PPI Guidelines:** The **Reserve Bank of India** issues **Master Directions** on **Prepaid Payment Instruments**, which regulate how companies can issue wallets and how they must store the money received from the **public**.
 
• **Digital Payment Ecosystem:** The integration of **fintech** within **Electric vehicle services** is part of a broader trend to streamline **micro-transactions**, though it introduces new layers of **regulatory risk** that the **RBI** monitors closely.

• **Interoperability:** A key feature discussed during the **2025** review was the potential requirement for **wallet interoperability**, allowing **EV** users to transfer balances between different charging or ride-hailing service providers.
 
• **Compliance Audits:** Companies in the **EV sector** are now required to submit periodic **System Audit Reports (SAR)** to the **RBI** to ensure their **digital payment** infrastructure meets **cybersecurity** and **financial safety** standards.
 
• **Financial Solvency:** The **central bank** has suggested that **non-banking entities** in the **Electric vehicle services** space might need to maintain higher **net worth** requirements to continue offering **wallet-based** services.

questions.question: In 2025, which country requested consultations with India at the World Trade Organization regarding trade measures on solar cells and modules?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**China**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In early **2025**, **China** formally requested consultations with **India** at the **World Trade Organization (WTO)** concerning India’s trade measures on **solar cells** and **solar modules**.
 
• This request marks the official commencement of a legal dispute within the **WTO dispute settlement framework**, where **China** challenged India's domestic protectionist policies.
 
• The primary focus of **China’s** complaint is the **Approved List of Models and Manufacturers (ALMM)** and the high **Basic Customs Duty (BCD)** imposed by the **Government of India**.
 
• **China** argues that these measures provide an unfair advantage to Indian domestic manufacturers and are inconsistent with **India’s** obligations under the **General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) 1994** and the **Agreement on Trade-Related Investment Measures (TRIMs)**.
 
• Consultations are the first stage of the **WTO** process, allowing the involved **member countries** to discuss the matter and find a solution without proceeding to formal litigation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Basic Customs Duty (BCD):** In **April 2022**, **India** implemented a **BCD** of **40%** on imported **solar modules** and **25%** on **solar cells** to reduce dependency on imports, particularly from **China**, and promote the **Atmanirbhar Bharat** initiative.
 
• **Approved List of Models and Manufacturers (ALMM):** Managed by the **Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE)**, this list ensures that only certified domestic manufacturers can supply components for government-subsidized projects, effectively acting as a **non-tariff barrier**.
 
• **Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme:** To support the local industry against foreign competition, **India** introduced the **PLI scheme** for **High-Efficiency Solar PV Modules** with an outlay of over **Rs. 24,000 crore**.
 
• **WTO Dispute Settlement Process:** If the consultations between **India** and **China** do not reach a resolution within **60 days**, **China** may request the **WTO** to establish a **dispute settlement panel** to adjudicate the matter.
 
• **India's Renewable Energy Target:** **India** has set an ambitious goal of reaching **500 GW** of non-fossil energy capacity by **2030**, making the solar supply chain a critical point of national economic interest.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Global Solar Market Dynamics:** **China** currently dominates over **80%** of the global **solar manufacturing supply chain**, leading to trade tensions not just with **India**, but also with the **United States** and the **European Union**.
 
• **Previous WTO Disputes:** **India** has previously lost a case at the **WTO** against the **USA** regarding **Domestic Content Requirements (DCR)** under the **Jawaharlal Nehru National Solar Mission** in **2016**.
 
• **Strategic Autonomy:** The **Indian government** maintains that these measures are essential for **energy security** and to prevent dumping of cheap components that could stifle the growth of nascent domestic industries.
 
• **Import Data:** Despite high duties, **India** remains a significant importer of solar components, with **imports from China** totaling billions of **US Dollars** annually due to the massive scale of Indian solar installations.

7f:T

questions.question: In 2025, India signed a $126.42 million loan agreement with which institution for the purpose of developing sustainable tourism infrastructure around Tehri Lake in Uttarakhand?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Asian Development Bank**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **January 2025**, the **Government of India** signed a **$126.42 million loan** agreement with the **Asian Development Bank (ADB)** to enhance the tourism potential of **Uttarakhand**.
 
• The primary objective of this loan is to develop **sustainable**, **inclusive**, and **climate-resilient tourism infrastructure** around the iconic **Tehri Lake** (Tehri Reservoir).
 
• The project, titled the **Integrated Tehri Lake Development Project**, aims to transform the region into a premier destination for **adventure tourism** and **water sports**.
 
• Key components of the agreement include the construction of a **world-class water sports academy**, **ferry terminals**, **eco-friendly resorts**, and **public amenities** to attract both domestic and international tourists.
 
• The project emphasizes **environmental sustainability** by integrating **solid waste management** systems and **sewage treatment plants** to protect the ecosystem of the **Bhagirathi River** and the reservoir.
 
• This initiative is expected to boost the **local economy** by creating **employment opportunities** for the **youth** and **women** of the **Tehri Garhwal** district through **skill development** programs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Asian Development Bank (ADB):**
 
 
• Established in **1966**, the **ADB** is a regional development bank headquartered in **Mandaluyong, Philippines**.
 
• As of **2025**, it has **69 member countries**, with **49** from within the **Asia-Pacific** region.
 
• The current President of **ADB** is **Masatsugu Asakawa**. Its main goal is to eradicate extreme poverty while promoting social and economic development.
 
 
 
• **Tehri Lake and Dam:**
 
 
• The **Tehri Dam** is the **highest dam in India** and one of the highest in the world, located on the **Bhagirathi River** in **Uttarakhand**.
 
• The **Tehri Reservoir**, often called **Tehri Lake**, is a massive man-made lake covering an area of approximately **42 square kilometers**.
 
• It is a significant source of **hydroelectric power** (with a capacity of **2,400 MW**) and provides drinking water and irrigation to several states in North India.
 
 
 
• **Tourism in Uttarakhand:**
 
 
• Known as **"Devbhoomi"** (Land of the Gods), **Uttarakhand** is a major hub for **spiritual tourism**, **trekking**, and **wildlife**.
 
• The state government has been focusing on **diversifying tourism** beyond religious circuits to include **wellness tourism** and **adventure sports** to increase the **GSDP (Gross State Domestic Product)**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Climate Resilience:** The project incorporates **climate-smart** design features to withstand the specific geographical challenges of the **Himalayan region**, such as landslides and seismic activity.
 
• **Institutional Support:** The **Department of Economic Affairs (DEA)** under the **Ministry of Finance** acted as the nodal agency for the **Government of India** in finalizing this **multilateral funding**.

questions.question: Which Indian Ministry released the first-ever monthly Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) in April 2025?

options.text: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)** released the first-ever **monthly Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS)** in **April 2025**, marking a significant shift in how labor data is tracked in India.
 
• The **National Sample Survey Office (NSSO)**, which is the statistical arm under **MoSPI**, is responsible for conducting these surveys and processing the data to reflect current employment trends.
 
• This move from **quarterly** (for urban areas) and **annual** reports to **monthly** reports was initiated to provide real-time insights into the Indian economy, allowing for more agile and evidence-based policy interventions.
 
• The **PLFS** serves as the primary source of official data on **employment** and **unemployment** indicators, including the **Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR)** and **Unemployment Rate (UR)** across various age groups and educational levels.
 
• The launch of the monthly series in **April 2025** aims to capture seasonal variations in the workforce more accurately, particularly in sectors like **agriculture** and **construction**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI):**
 
 
• It came into existence as an independent Ministry on **15th October 1999** after the merger of the Department of Statistics and the Department of Programme Implementation.
 
• The Ministry has two wings: one relating to **Statistics** and the other relating to **Programme Implementation**.
 
• The **National Statistical Office (NSO)** consists of the **Central Statistical Office (CSO)** and the **National Sample Survey Office (NSSO)**.
 
 
 
• **Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS):**
 
 
• The **PLFS** was launched by the **NSO** in **April 2017** to estimate the key employment and unemployment indicators in a shorter time interval for urban areas and annually for both rural and urban areas.
 
• It uses a **rotational panel sampling** design in urban areas to measure short-term changes in labor indicators.
 
• Before **2017**, the **NSSO** used to conduct quinquennial (every five years) surveys on employment and unemployment.
 
 
 
• **Important Labor Indicators:**
 
 
• **Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR):** It is defined as the percentage of persons in the **labour force** (working or seeking or available for work) in the population.
 
• **Worker Population Ratio (WPR):** It is defined as the percentage of **employed persons** in the population.
 
• **Unemployment Rate (UR):** It is defined as the percentage of persons **unemployed** among the persons in the labour force.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **NSSO Functions:** The **National Sample Survey Office** is mandated to conduct large-scale sample surveys in diverse fields on an **all-India basis**. It plays a vital role in providing data for the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDG)** monitoring framework.
 
• **Data Frequency:** The transition to **monthly releases** in **2025** aligns India with global best practices followed by developed economies like the **USA** and **European Union** countries, where labor data is a monthly high-frequency indicator.
 
• **Policy Impact:** High-frequency labor data helps the **Ministry of Finance** and the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** in making critical decisions regarding **monetary policy** and **fiscal stimulus** by identifying stress in the labor market early.
 
• **National Statistical Commission (NSC):** The **NSC** is an autonomous body formed in **June 2005** under the recommendation of the **Rangarajan Commission** to reduce the problems faced by statistical agencies in the country regarding data collection.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following missions is the first space-based Indian mission to study the sun?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aditya L1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Aditya-L1** is the first space-based **Indian mission** to study the **Sun**. It is an observatory-class mission designed to provide a comprehensive understanding of solar dynamics.
 
• The spacecraft was successfully launched by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** on **September 2, 2023**, using the **PSLV-C57** launch vehicle.
 
• The mission is positioned in a **halo orbit** around the **Lagrange point 1 (L1)** of the Sun-Earth system, which is located approximately **1.5 million kilometers** from Earth.
 
• Being placed at the **L1 point** allows the satellite to observe the **Sun** continuously without any **occultation** or **eclipses**, providing a major advantage in monitoring solar activities in real-time.
 
• The primary scientific objectives include studying the **solar corona** (the outermost layer), the **chromosphere**, and the **photosphere**, as well as investigating **coronal mass ejections (CMEs)**, **solar flares**, and **space weather**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **AstroSat**:
 
 
• Launched in **September 2015**, it is India’s first dedicated **multi-wavelength space observatory**.
 
• It carries five scientific payloads to observe the universe in **Optical, Ultraviolet, and X-ray** regions of the electromagnetic spectrum simultaneously.
 
 
 
• **Chandrayaan-1**:
 
 
• Launched in **October 2008** via **PSLV-C11**, it was India's first mission to the **Moon**.
 
• The mission is famous for discovering the presence of **water molecules (H2O)** and **hydroxyl (OH)** on the lunar surface.
 
 
 
• **Mangalyaan (Mars Orbiter Mission)**:
 
 
• Launched on **November 5, 2013**, it was India’s first **interplanetary mission**.
 
• India became the **first nation** to reach the Martian orbit in its **maiden attempt** and the fourth space agency in the world to reach **Mars**.
 
 
 
• **Lagrange Points**:
 
 
• These are specific positions in space where the **gravitational pull** of two large masses precisely equals the **centripetal force** required for a small object to move with them.
 
• There are **five Lagrange points** (L1 to L5) for the Sun-Earth system. **L1** is the most significant for solar observations.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Scientific Payloads of Aditya L1**:
 
 
• The spacecraft carries **seven payloads**. Four of these are **remote sensing payloads** (VELC, SUIT, SoLEXS, HEL1OS) that look directly at the Sun.
 
• The other three are **in-situ payloads** (ASPEX, PAPA, Advanced Tri-axial High Resolution Digital Magnetometers) that study the local environment at the **L1 point**.
 
 
 
• **Visible Emission Line Coronagraph (VELC)**: This is the primary payload designed by the **Indian Institute of Astrophysics (IIA)**, **Bengaluru**, to study the solar corona and the dynamics of **coronal mass ejections**.
 
• **Solar Ultraviolet Imaging Telescope (SUIT)**: Developed by the **Inter-University Centre for Astronomy and Astrophysics (IUCAA)**, **Pune**, it images the solar **photosphere** and **chromosphere** in near **Ultraviolet** wavelengths.
 
• The mission duration is expected to be approximately **5 years**, providing long-term data on the **11-year solar cycle**.
</ul

questions.question: In the context of 2025 discussions on global governance and foreign-policy literacy, which of the following books by Richard Haass is widely cited as a concise primer that helps general readers understand world politics and major global challenges?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The World: A Brief Introduction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The World: A Brief Introduction**, published in **2020**, is written by **Richard Haass** to address the "gap" in **foreign-policy literacy** among the general public.
 
• The book serves as a concise primer that explains the essential history, geography, and **political science** concepts necessary to understand the modern world.
 
• It covers the evolution of the international system starting from the **Peace of Westphalia** in **1648**, through the **World Wars** and the **Cold War**, up to the current era of **globalization**.
 
• The text details major global challenges such as **climate change**, **cybersecurity**, **pandemics**, and **nuclear proliferation**, making it a critical resource for **2025** discussions on **global governance**.
 
• Haass argues that in an interconnected world, an informed citizenry is vital for a functioning democracy, as domestic stability is increasingly linked to international events.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Richard Haass:** 
 
 
• He is an American diplomat who served as the **President** of the **Council on Foreign Relations (CFR)** for twenty years, from **2003** to **2023**.
 
• He has held senior positions in the **U.S. State Department** and served as a special assistant to President **George H.W. Bush**.
 
 
 
• **The New Map: Energy, Climate, and the Clash of Nations:** 
 
 
• This book was authored by **Daniel Yergin** in **2020**.
 
• It focuses on how the **shale revolution** and the transition to **renewable energy** are altering the **geopolitical** landscape between the **United States**, **Russia**, and **China**.
 
 
 
• **The Long Game: China's Grand Strategy to Displace American Order:** 
 
 
• Written by **Rush Doshi** and published in **2021**.
 
• It provides an analysis of **China's** long-term strategic intentions to reshape the **global order**.
 
 
 
• **The Future Is Asian:** 
 
 
• Authored by **Parag Khanna** in **2019**.
 
• It explores the "Asianization" of the world, highlighting the **economic** and **cultural** pivot toward the **Asian continent** in the **21st century**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **World Order:** A central theme in **Richard Haass's** work is the maintenance of **international order** and the prevention of **global disarray**.
 
• **Bill of Obligations:** In **2023**, Haass released **"The Bill of Obligations: The Ten Habits of Good Citizens,"** which shifts the focus toward domestic civic responsibilities in the **United States**.
 
• **Foreign Policy Literacy:** The concept refers to the basic knowledge required to evaluate how a country interacts with the world, a skill Haass considers mandatory for **voters** in the modern era.
 
• **Council on Foreign Relations (CFR):** Founded in **1921**, it is one of the most influential **think tanks** in the world specializing in **U.S. foreign policy** and **international affairs**.
</ul
